headline: Nous Research, maker of the open-source Hermes Agent, has confirmed a $90 million funding round that values it at $1.5 billion.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: the confirmation was published on 7 Oct 2026, before the 8 Oct window.
importance_line: What changed is that a free, open-source AI agent is becoming a paid product for businesses, which matters to the developers who use it and to companies that want agents without sending their data to a vendor, then to rival agent makers, and the doubt is that the usage and revenue figures are the company's own estimates and press reports.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Nous Research confirmed a $90 million Series B round (a mid-stage investment round) led by Robot Ventures, with Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Samsung and 1789 Capital taking part, bringing its total funding to $158 million and paying for "Hermes for Businesses", which lets companies run customized AI agents on multi-step tasks while keeping their data private. By the startup's own estimates Hermes Agent has been cloned more than 24 million times and drives roughly 2.5% of global AI token usage (tokens are the units of text AI models process), and the Wall Street Journal reported annualized revenue of about $36 million in mid-September.
notes: The pool item was The AI Insider (8 Oct), which rewrites the TechCrunch story of 7 Oct; the original outlet is credited. The Wall Street Journal first reported the round.
